## My two picks

### Tonight, Mon. Sept. 28 — business dinner: **Mooo…. Beacon Hill**
**Why it fits:** This is the more appropriate of the two for a polished client dinner: a modern steakhouse in the XV Beacon at **15 Beacon St**, with an elegant, relatively intimate setting, serious wine list, and professional service rather than a showy “scene.” It is a distinctly different experience from the anniversary choice. Google’s current listing shows reservations are required, private dining is available, and lists it at **$100+ per person**—well within your stated ceiling even with top cuts and wine.

- Restaurant/site: https://www.mooorestaurant.com/beacon-hill/
- Live booking page: https://www.opentable.com/r/mooo-beacon-hill-boston
- Phone: **617-670-2515**

**Availability check:** I could not obtain the actual live OpenTable slots because OpenTable blocked access in this browser, so I can’t honestly call a 6:30–8:00 opening confirmed. The restaurant is listed as open through **9:00 p.m. on Monday**. For an important client meal, I’d open the booking page or call now and request **7:00/7:30 for two**, noting that a quieter table is important.

### Tomorrow, Tue. Sept. 29 — anniversary: **SRV**
**Why it fits:** SRV is a warm, Venetian-style Italian restaurant in the South End, focused on cicchetti, fresh pasta made from locally milled flour, made-to-order risotto, Italian wine, and Italian-inspired cocktails. It is not a splashy expense-account dining room; it is more intimate and food-led, and makes a nicely contrasting anniversary evening after a steakhouse client dinner. It is Italian rather than specifically seafood-first, so I would inspect the current menu before committing if seafood is essential.

- Restaurant/site and menu: https://www.srvboston.com/
- Current booking page: https://resy.com/cities/boston-ma/venues/srv
- Phone: **617-536-9500**
- Address: **569 Columbus Ave., Boston**

**Availability check:** Resy’s current result says there is **no online availability today**, but that its **next availability for two is tomorrow**. That makes it a realistic option for Tuesday, although the result did not expose the exact times; use the live Resy page to target your 6:30–8:00 range. SRV says reservations are released 28 days ahead and can also be made by phone between 2 and 9 p.m. daily. Tuesday dinner service is listed as **5–9 p.m.**

## If Italian seafood is the priority: **Mamma Maria** (best-style alternative for the anniversary)
Mamma Maria in North Square is the more literal match for a romantic, distinctly Boston Italian seafood anniversary: it occupies a historic North End townhouse, has very small rooms (including a room for two), and its current sample menu includes **baked Duxbury oysters**, **Maine lobster agnolotti**, and line-caught black bass. The official site describes its seasonal focus as moving toward summer seafood, and it has the historic cobblestone/North End setting you may be looking for.

- Site: https://www.mammamaria.com/
- Current menu: https://www.mammamaria.com/menu/
- Live booking page: https://www.sevenrooms.com/reservations/mammamaria
- Phone: **617-523-0077**
- Address: **3 North Square, Boston**

**Availability check:** I ran its live SevenRooms search for **tonight, 2 people, 7:00 p.m.** and it returned **“Unfortunately there is no availability at the selected time.”** I could not reliably switch its embedded date control to tomorrow in this browser, so I cannot represent Tuesday as available. It is still the first alternate I would check for Tuesday if the precise romantic Italian-seafood brief outranks the live availability signal at SRV.

## One to skip for these dates
**Ostra** would otherwise be a strong seafood-led upscale alternative—its current menu listing includes lobster gnocchetti and salt-crusted branzino for two—but current search results report it is **closed for a private event on Tuesday, Sept. 29**. So it should not be your anniversary fallback tomorrow.

- Site/menu: https://ostraboston.com/ostra-menu
- Reservations: https://www.opentable.com/r/ostra-boston

**Practical order:** Try **Mooo for tonight** immediately; book **SRV tomorrow** if its times suit; if the anniversary needs to be seafood-forward, check **Mamma Maria’s SevenRooms page** immediately afterward and call if its online calendar is opaque.

conversation.text:
I’m in Boston with my wife for the next two evenings on a work trip, and I’d like help narrowing this down carefully. We need two quite different dinner choices: one polished, quiet, high-end place appropriate for taking clients, and a separate restaurant for our anniversary that feels genuinely romantic—Italian seafood would be especially appealing, or something distinctly Boston.

Could you check current information rather than relying on reviews alone, including whether either has a realistic reservation opening in the next two days? I am comfortable up to roughly $500 per person for the business dinner, but do not want something flashy just for the sake of it. Please give me the restaurant sites or current booking pages as well, since I will want to look over the menus and photos myself.

I can check live openings, but what party size and approximate preferred dinner time should I use for each evening (and should I treat “next two evenings” as tonight, Sept. 28, and tomorrow, Sept. 29, Boston time)?

Yes, please use tonight, September 28, and tomorrow, September 29, Boston time. It will be just the two of us. Ideally around 7:00 or 7:30 p.m. for each dinner, though I would consider anything roughly between 6:30 and 8:00 if that is what is available.

R1.reason: The agent chose Mooo Beacon Hill and reported a $100+ price level, but no Michelin Guide or equivalent fine-dining listing visibly showing its cuisine/style and price indicators was left open, and the user never specified Michelin Guide.

R2.reason: The selected anniversary restaurant was SRV, but no usable OpenTable listing for SRV was opened or left open (the only OpenTable tabs were access-denied pages for other restaurants), and the user did not request OpenTable specifically.

R3.reason: Although the answer states Mooo is $100+ and says it could not confirm a reservation, no open official/current Mooo page visibly provides the required client-dining evidence together with a reservation interface or next-two-days availability evidence.

R4.reason: The answer describes SRV as an anniversary choice and reports an unverified availability claim, but it does not report SRV's expected price level and no SRV booking/listing page with visible romantic/special-occasion and availability evidence was left open.
